'''David John Rose''' (May 8, 1922 - October 24, 1985) was a Canadian born- American [[nuclear engineering|nuclear engineer]] and [[environmentalist]]. 

He was a professor of nuclear energy at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] and a consultant for the [[Environmental Protection Agency]]. 

== Education ==

Rose received a B.A.Sc. degree in engineering physics from the University of British Columbia in 1947 and a Ph.D. degree in physics from MIT in 1950. He joined the faculty of the Department of Nuclear Engineering at MIT when it was formed in 1958.

== Work history ==

Rose served as captain in the Canadian artillery from 1942 to 1947. He worked at [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]] until joining the MIT Nuclear Engineering faculty in 1958. He led the development of the department's program in plasmas and controlled [[Fusion power|fusion]], and was on the MIT faculty for the rest of his professional career. From 1969 to 1971, during a two-year leave of absence, he worked at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]], where he was the first director of their office of Long-range planning.

Rose's career was said to have three phases: scientist and engineer; technology/policy analyst; and "bridge builder" between scientific and theological communities.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://web.mit.edu/nse/events/rose-lecture.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110315060630/http://web.mit.edu/nse/events/rose-lecture.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2011-03-15|title=Seminars {{!}} MIT Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering|date=2011-03-15|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref>

== Publications, testimony and other history ==

Rose wrote over 150 articles<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dspace.mit.edu/browse?authority=e640a0057974312fab073056097d1e64&type=author|title=Browsing by Author "Rose, David J."|website=dspace.mit.edu|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dspace.mit.edu/browse?rpp=20&offset=20&etal=-1&authority=8fa7da21020f8ce7e3a3d5c0f931affa&sort_by=-1&type=author&order=ASC|title=Browsing by Author "Rose, D. J."|website=dspace.mit.edu|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref> ranging from high technology to theology. He was author of the widely cited ''Plasmas and Controlled Fusion'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mitpress.mit.edu/books/plasmas-and-controlled-fusion|title=Plasmas and Controlled Fusion {{!}} The MIT Press|last=Press|first=The MIT|website=mitpress.mit.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref> with Melville Clark, which became the standard textbook in the field of fusion energy.<ref name=":0" />

In 1975 Rose taught the MIT Nuclear Engineering Department's first course on sustainable energy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.mit.edu/nse/about/history.html|title=MIT NSE: History|website=web.mit.edu|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref>

He testified to Congress in 1977.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Technology|first=United States Congress House Committee on Science and|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=454qAAAAMAAJ&dq=david+j+rose&pg=PA328|title=1978 ERDA Authorization: Hearing Before the Committee on Science and Technology, U.S. House of Representatives, Ninety-fifth Congress, First Session|date=1977|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office|pages=328–356, 469–471|language=en}}</ref> He was the primary author of ''Learning about Energy'',<ref>{{Cite book|last=Rose|first=David J|url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/version/229766034|title=Learning about energy|date=1986|publisher=New York, New York : Springer Science+Business Media, LLC|isbn=978-1-4757-5647-0|edition=1st ed. 1986|language=en}}</ref> published posthumously in 1986.<ref name=":0" />

Rose was thesis supervisor for [[Richard K. Lester]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Laser isotope separation for uranium enrichment : a technology assessment|url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/17152|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|date=1979|degree=Thesis|first=Richard K. (Richard Keith)|last=Lester|hdl=1721.1/17152}}</ref>

Shortly before his death, and days before he was hospitalized, Rose wrote an article opposing [[Strategic Defense Initiative|Star Wars (SDI)]] and asking for support for a petition against it.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tech.mit.edu/V105/N50/rose.50o.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120808075559/http://tech.mit.edu/V105/N50/rose.50o.html|url-status=dead|title=Work toward peace, oppose Star Wars - The Tech|archive-date=2012-08-08|access-date=2020-03-30|volume=105|issue=50|date=1985-11-19}}</ref>

== Honors, Awards and recognitions ==

* Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences
* Fellow of the American Physical Society
* Fellow of the American Academy for the Advancement of Science. 
* 1975 Arthur Holly Compton Award of the American Nuclear Society for excellence in teaching<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://killianlectures.mit.edu/david-j-rose|title=Killian Lectures, David J. Rose|website=MIT Killian Lectures|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref>
* [[James Rhyne Killian|James R Killian Jr]] Faculty Achievement Award and lecturer in 1979–80
* 1984 David J. Rose Lecture was established in his honor, to recognize his work in fusion technology, energy and environment impact, nuclear waste management, and ethical issues of science and technology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.mit.edu/2013/david-j-rose-lectureship-nuclear-technology|title=The David J. Rose Lectureship in Nuclear Technology|website=MIT News|date=3 March 2013 |access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Waugh|first=John|url=https://killianlectures.mit.edu/sites/default/files/images/Killian%20Citation%20D%20Rose.pdf|title=Report of the Killian Award Selection Committee|date=May 16, 1979|access-date=2020-03-30|archive-date=2024-08-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811092614/http://killianlectures.mit.edu/sites/default/files/images/Killian%20Citation%20D%20Rose.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 1986 Fusion Power Associates established an annual prize for excellence in fusion engineering in Rose's honor.<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life and death==
Rose was divorced from his first marriage, with whom he had three children, a daughter Elizabeth and two sons, Hugh and Andrew. His second marriage was to Renate Papke. <ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1985/10/30/us/david-john-rose-63-is-dead-nuclear-researcher-at-mit.html NYT OBITUARY]</ref>

Rose retired in December 1984, and moved to Honolulu, HI.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tech.mit.edu/V105/PDF/V105-N45.pdf|title=David J. Rose|date=1985-10-25|publisher=The Tech|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810201545/http://tech.mit.edu/V105/PDF/V105-N45.pdf|archive-date=2014-08-10|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref>

Rose died on October 24, 1985 from [[emphasema]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1985/10/30/us/david-john-rose-63-is-dead-nuclear-researcher-at-mit.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524181632/https://www.nytimes.com/1985/10/30/us/david-john-rose-63-is-dead-nuclear-researcher-at-mit.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2015-05-24|title=David John Rose, 63, Is Dead - Nuclear Researcher at M.I.T. - NYTimes.com|website=[[The New York Times]]|date=2015-05-24|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref>

In the 2026 Tom McCarthy film ''[[A Statement]]'', he is portrayed by actor [[John Turturro]]. <ref>[https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/a-statement-review-tom-mccarthy-1235220103/ A Statement film review]</ref>
